title: Reuse contract with open-data-datasheets and ewing-open-data-catalog (M0 exit criterion)
context: PLAN.md v0.2 establishes an explicit reuse contract as an M0 exit criterion: this project consumes (never re-implements) the canonical model, Croissant validator, and bounded inspection protocol from the sibling project open-data-datasheets. ewing-open-data-catalog consumes and links the datasheets produced here. Without a committed reuse contract, the three sibling projects risk triplication-drift where separate validators diverge -- identified as a medium/medium risk in the updated risk table. This task is not about tracking external reuse events (reuse-021); it is about the binding internal dependency/ownership contract between the three Elyos sibling projects. Binding cancer guardrails apply.
objective: Document the binding reuse contract between cancer-dataset-datasheets, open-data-datasheets (shared toolkit owner), and ewing-open-data-catalog (consumer), specifying which components are shared dependencies vs. cancer-specific extensions, who owns the shared core, and the no-parallel-reimplementation rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Contract document committed to /docs/sibling-reuse-contract.md specifying which components (canonical model, Croissant validator, inspection protocol) are consumed from open-data-datasheets as a dependency and not reimplemented here.

Cancer-specific extensions (genomic-privacy gate, identifiability scanner, cancer-license matrix, shareAlike flag, upstreamVersionDoi) listed as this project's supersets not re-implemented in sibling projects.
ewing-open-data-catalog's role as a downstream consumer (links datasheets produced here; does not re-document datasets already covered here) is explicitly recorded.
No-parallel-reimplementation rule stated: any change to shared toolkit components routes through open-data-datasheets, never as a cancer-dataset-datasheets fork.
Contract cross-referenced from PLAN.md dependencies section and from canonical-metadata-model.md.
